newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., urges judge to OK arena deal.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., urges judge to OK arena deal.

text.p: Attorneys for the city of Sacramento will make their closing arguments in court on Tuesday in their bid to sell up to $80 million of notes to refinance a local basketball arena.
The trial in Superior Court in Sacramento began on Monday. The judge hearing the case is expected to hear final arguments later Tuesday and issue a written ruling in the coming days.

In April, the city of Sacramento asked the court to "validate" the proposed note sale. City attorneys said the validation process would clear away the legal challenges facing the deal and allow the city to quickly issue the notes.
The Sacramento City Council approved the note plan in February in order to keep the National Basketball Association's Sacramento Kings playing in the city.
With the proceeds of the note sale, the city would refinance $51.5 million of Arco Arena debt, where the Kings play. The remaining note proceeds would be used to refinance other franchise debts.
The notes were expected to be sold in April. But the deal was put on hold after at least two lawsuits were filed against the city's proposal.
If the Superior Court judge validated the deal, attorneys for the city said they would ask the court to dismiss the lawsuits.
